name: Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing Ltd
tagline: Niche aero/defense/nuclear precision-tooling maker with 65% gross margins, a Rs 887 Cr nuclear order book and Saudi-JV optionality - but ~104x P/E, FY26 earnings down, ROCE compressed to ~11% and QIP dilution pending

fundamentals_narrative: Unimech makes precision tooling (jigs, fixtures, tools), aero-engine tooling and now bellows for global aerospace/defense OEMs, and has added a large Indian nuclear-tooling order book. The prior thin write-up's 'ROE 22.6% / ROCE 21.4% / +71% growth' picture has weakened materially: FY26 revenue was flat at Rs 240.5 Cr, EBITDA fell 18% to Rs 75 Cr and PAT dropped to Rs 63 Cr (from Rs 83.5 Cr) on 'planned investments'; screener now shows ROCE ~11% and latest ROE ~8%. TTM reported profit also carries ~Rs 43 Cr of other/treasury income (IPO proceeds), so underlying operating earnings are lower than the headline. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 198 Cr looks strong but ~21% of it is the newly acquired Hobel Bellows (2 months only); standalone was ~Rs 108 Cr (+71% off a Rs 63 Cr base). Gross margin 65%, EBITDA margin 36.5%, PAT Rs 28 Cr (+46%). The setup is genuinely interesting - Rs 887 Cr of nuclear orders, a 5-year FACC Austria supply deal, a 51:49 Saudi machining JV, and only 58% capacity utilisation - but the stock trades at ~104x trailing earnings and a QIP plus MPS-driven promoter sell-down are coming, with working-capital days rising to 160+ and gross debt set to double.

bull_case: Genuine niche with qualification moats - precision aero-engine tooling / jigs / fixtures for global OEMs, 65% gross margin, 36% EBITDA margin; import-substitution tailwind
Large new growth vector: Rs 887 Cr cumulative nuclear-sector order wins (~3x current annual revenue), execution from H2FY27; plus a 5-year USD 7.5M FACC Austria supply agreement
Only 58% capacity utilisation - substantial operating-leverage headroom before fresh capex is needed for the core business
Optionality from the 51:49 Saudi (Dammam) machining JV for Middle-East energy/utility, and the Hobel Bellows acquisition (AS9100 target Q4FY27, 15-20% growth)
Very high promoter holding (79.8%) - strong alignment (though it must come down to <=75%)
bear_case: Valuation is extreme - ~104x trailing P/E, ~10x book - on a Rs 285 Cr revenue base; any multiple de-rating would hurt badly
FY26 was a down year: revenue -1%, EBITDA -18%, PAT ~Rs 63 Cr vs Rs 83.5 Cr; ROCE compressed to ~11%, latest ROE ~8% - the 'excellent fundamentals' framing is stale
TTM reported profit is padded by ~Rs 43 Cr of other/treasury income (IPO proceeds); other income fell to Rs 7 Cr in Q1 from Rs 15 Cr - underlying operating earnings are lower and this tailwind fades
Supply/dilution overhang: up to Rs 750 Cr QIP approved and promoter must sell down from 79.8% to <=75% within 18 months
Lumpy execution (Q3FY26 was near-zero: Rs 34 Cr revenue, Rs 2 Cr PAT); working-capital days rising to 160+, gross debt guided to double by FY27 - a cash-hungry ramp
Nuclear order execution is unproven at this scale; US tariff risk on aero exports (partly mitigated via FTWZ / geographic diversification)
verdict_headline: Real niche and a genuinely large new order book, but priced at ~104x with FY26 earnings down, returns compressed, profit partly treasury-fed, and dilution pending
verdict_reasoning: The business is a legitimate high-margin precision-tooling niche with qualification moats, and the Rs 887 Cr nuclear book plus FACC/Saudi optionality is a real forward vector
But the deep read punctures the prior 'excellent fundamentals' tagline: FY26 revenue flat, EBITDA -18%, PAT down, ROCE ~11%, ROE ~8%, and ~Rs 43 Cr of TTM profit is other/treasury income
Q1FY27's headline +71% is flattered by the Hobel acquisition (21% of revenue, 2 months); standalone growth is strong but off a tiny base
At ~104x trailing P/E with a QIP and MPS sell-down coming, working capital rising to 160+ days and gross debt doubling, the valuation prices in near-flawless multi-vector execution
Conviction eased to Medium; thesis_fit to neither - 10x from a Rs 7,500 Cr / 104x base in 2-3 years is not a credible path, whatever the order book

Can working capital at 160+ days and doubling gross debt be funded without further raises beyond the QIP?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium. The deep read is net negative on the current picture: FY26 earnings fell, ROCE/ROE compressed to ~11%/~8%, reported profit is partly treasury income, execution is lumpy, and a QIP + MPS sell-down loom - all against a ~104x P/E. Offsetting positives (Rs 887 Cr nuclear book, FACC, Saudi JV, 58% utilisation) are real but forward and unproven, so conviction eases rather than collapses.
